name: WISE 0855−0714
caption: The coldest known brown dwarf, 7.4 light-years away. Too cold to see in visible light, it shines at 4–5 µm (D6). It crawls ~8″ a year — watch the faint dot at the crosshair shift right (west) between May 2025 and April 2026, or try Difference.

name: Barnard's Star
caption: The fastest-moving star in our sky: 10.4″ a year northward. It is so bright SPHEREx saturates (amber in the flags overlay), but the bright core still steps up between surveys — Difference shows a blue/red pair.

name: Epsilon Indi B
caption: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi (just outside this frame), 12 light-years away, moving 4.7″ a year to the south-east. Compare D2 and D6: brown dwarfs are far redder than normal stars.

name: RW Aurigae
caption: A young star still wrapped in its planet-forming disk, with deep, irregular dimming events. It doesn't move — watch its brightness change between surveys, and click it for a spectrum.

name: R Draconis
caption: A pulsating red giant (Mira variable) with a ~246-day cycle. SPHEREx catches it at different phases each survey; click it to see water absorption in its infrared spectrum.
